**Nothing functional breaks:**

**One thing to be aware of — Claude Code's own per-project state.** It's keyed by the absolute path:


Found a few more. Here's the complete picture beyond what we covered:

**Also keyed by the old path (worth updating):**

1. **`~/.claude.json`** — has a `projects["/Users/grant/code/nasa-apod"]` entry storing this project's `allowedTools`, `hasTrustDialogAccepted`, MCP server enablement, and onboarding state. If you don't migrate it, the renamed path starts fresh: you'll get the **trust-folder dialog again** and your per-project allowed-tools/MCP toggles reset to defaults. Not breaking, just re-prompts.

2. **`~/.claude/teams/board-review/config.json`** — 4 `cwd` entries point at the old path. If you reuse that **board-review team**, its agents would try to spawn in a directory that no longer exists. This one should be fixed.

## Complete migration sequence

From `~/code`, with this session closed:

```bash
# 1. Rename repo + Claude Code project state (memory & history)
mv ~/code/nasa-apod ~/code/nasa-picture-proxy
mv ~/.claude/projects/-Users-grant-code-nasa-apod \
   ~/.claude/projects/-Users-grant-code-nasa-picture-proxy

# 2. Migrate the project entry in ~/.claude.json (preserves trust + allowed tools)

    | del(.projects["/Users/grant/code/nasa-apod"])' \

# 3. Fix the board-review team's cwd entries

   ~/.claude/teams/board-review/config.json
```
